title: Concurrent tool calls lose evidence and duplicate issue numbers (no lock, read-modify-write)
where: JarlSkill skills/jarl/scripts/jarl.mjs:308 (id = max+1), :432/:438 (evidence read-modify-write), :218 (decisions rewrite), :343-352 (set); SKILL.md:284-286
evidence: Scratch loop jarl-a: 20 parallel `evidence 005 --ran wN --saw ok` → `rows in file: 14`, `log lines: 19`, one call failed with `no such issue: 005` (it read a half-written file). 10 parallel `new "pN"` → `4 006, 2 007, 2 008, 2 009` (duplicate numbers; findIssue then returns the first match). SKILL.md already admits it: "confirm it reads `done` — a write that silently failed to land is worse than one that never ran, and it has happened." The loop's model has workers, reviewer and merger all writing through the tool with --root at the same time (SKILL.md:190, 277). In this loop up to seven Opus workers ran at once (a working note of 2026-09-23).
proposal: Serialize every mutating command behind `.jarl/.lock`: openSync(path,'wx') with a short retry/backoff and a stale-lock timeout. Write files to a temp file and rename them into place. `new` creates its file with the 'wx' flag and retries under the next number on EEXIST. Add a node:test that starts 20 child processes. Cost: ~40-60 lines plus one test, zero dependencies. Done when rerunning the experiment gives 20 rows and 20 log lines, and 10 parallel `new` calls give 10 distinct numbers.

v.reason: I re-ran it in a scratch loop (scratchpad/research/skeptic-jarl) and it came out worse than reported. 20 parallel `evidence 001 --ran wN --saw ok` left 1 row and 2 log lines, and 18 calls failed with `no such issue: 001`: the writes read a half-written file. 10 parallel `new` gave `4× 001, 2× 002, 2× 003, 2× 004`. The code matches the claim: jarl.mjs:308 computes max+1, evidence does readFileSync→setSection→writeFileSync, and there is no lock. SKILL.md:285 admits a silently lost write 'has happened'. The real loop has no duplicate ids today, because the coordinator did most writes serially. The skill still tells workers, the reviewer and the merger to write concurrently through --root, so the defect is by design. The fix is small and sound.

title: Argument parser swallows values that start with -- ; `--ran "--help"` exits 0 having recorded nothing; unknown flags silently ignored
where: jarl.mjs:821-833 (parseArgs: `!next.startsWith('--')`), :843 (flags.help → exit 0)
evidence:
Scratch jarl-a:
(1) `evidence 001 "--json prints ok"` → `evidence requires "<what was run..."`, exit 1.
(2) `--ran "yg check" --saw "--- FAIL: 3 pairs"` → `a row needs both --ran ... and --saw ..., each with a value`, exit 1.
(3) `--ran "--help" --saw usage` → prints the full USAGE and exits 0 with no row written, a silent success for any script.
(4) `new "--json output drops key"` → `new requires "<title>"`.
(5) `evidence 001 -- "--json..."` → still refused: there is no `--` terminator.
(6) `new d --kidn gap` → filed as `Kind: bug`, exit 0.
These are exactly the outputs a Yggdrasil loop has to quote: CLI flags, `--json` output, test runner lines starting with `---`.
proposal: Give each command a table of known flags. A value flag always consumes the next argv entry, whatever it starts with. Support `--flag=value` and a bare `--` that ends option parsing. An unknown flag is an error that names the valid ones. `--help` counts only when it is not the value of another flag. Cost: ~50 lines plus table-driven tests. Done when the six cases above record correctly or fail loudly, and `--ran --help` never exits 0 without writing.

v.reason: Reproduced: `evidence 002 --ran "--help" --saw usage` exits 0 and writes no row; `new d --kidn gap` files silently with exit 0; `evidence 002 "--json prints ok"` is refused. parseArgs at jarl.mjs:829 is as quoted. Most cases fail loudly, though (exit 1 with a message). The silent ones are only `--help` swallowed as a value and unknown flags, so I lowered it to medium. The proposal (a flag table, `--`, `--flag=value`, unknown flag = error) is sound and cheap.

title: The `done` gate is satisfied without proving anything: filing-time notes count as evidence, self-approves count as review, and a reopen keeps the old approve
where: jarl.mjs:341-342 (evidence non-empty + approve newer than last round), :552-563 (reviewState ignores status changes), :570-582 (review has no reviewer identity)
evidence: 70 issues had evidence from birth: first evidence line `Source: …` (translated from Polish) (grep across issues = 70), written at filing time (e.g. log:1425-1431, 00:32, same minute as `filed`). So the done gate's evidence check was met before any work began. Review provenance over 221 approves (log): 82 `Coordinator:`, ~115 `Own review…`, ~16 `Fresh reviewer` (labels translated from Polish). The typical sequence is a coordinator approve and `→ done` in the same minute (log:1461-1462). Scratch: `review 001 approve; set done; set in-progress; set done` → exit 0, no new review needed after the reopen. The 209 episode depended on this: it was closed on another issue's evidence and reopened, and nothing forced a fresh review.
proposal:
Keep self-review legal, since the ruling on working without subagents allowed it, but make it visible and make stale proofs expire.
(a) `review <id> approve --by <fresh:model|self|jarl>`, recorded in the log line.
(b) `set done` needs at least one --ran/--saw row written after the issue's last `→ in-progress`.
(c) Any transition out of done spends the approve, as a round does.
(d) `report` prints `done N · fresh review a · self b`.
Cost: ~60 lines plus tests. Done when replaying 203's history is refused at `done` until a post-in-progress row exists, and `report` on this loop shows the 16/204 split.

v.reason: Scope it to what B3 does not cover. First, a reopen keeps the old approve, reproduced: `review approve; set done; set in-progress; set done` gives exit 0, and reviewState (jarl.mjs:552-563) looks only at rounds. Second, filing-time evidence satisfies the done gate: 70 issues carry an `Źródło:` line, and cmdSet:341 checks only that evidence is non-empty. Drop the review-provenance parts (a) and (d); they belong to B3. Caution on (b), 'a row after the last → in-progress': 87 of 220 done issues never passed through in-progress (verified). The rule needs a defined behaviour for those, e.g. rows after filing when there is no in-progress line. Medium, not high: the gate is weak but has not been shown to hide a bad merge beyond the 209 episode.

evidence: Log analysis: 503 of 1241 evidence/evidence-row/review/done lines are identical same-minute writes across several issues (104 groups). title: Merge SHA and CI state live in free text; `merged` log step almost never used; no 'merged, CI pending' state
where: SKILL.md:277-283 (merger step 4: evidence text + `log "merged <id> <sha>"`); jarl.mjs has no merge field
evidence: `merged ` occurs 4 times in log.md against 221 `→ done`. Merge SHAs and CI runs appear only inside evidence prose, e.g. log:1450 `scalone 356d8a5b, push; CI 35943958049 w toku`, then log:1460 `evidence row · gh run watch 35943958049`, then `→ done`. proposal: `merged <ids…> --sha <sha> [--ci <run-id>]` writes **Merged:** and **CI:** fields plus a log line. `status` shows a `merged, CI pending` count. `set done` checks with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <base>` in the issue's Repo that the SHA is on the release branch. `report` lists the SHA per issue for the changelog. title: Research-to-issue import with stable, global finding ids and a coverage view
where: JarlSkill skills/jarl/scripts/jarl.mjs:297-316 (cmdNew), :180-205 (renderIssue); research/2026-09-2*/findings.json; issues 152 and 129 of the 6.1.0 loop
evidence: Eight 2026-09-23..25 reports hold 437 verified findings in findings.json. Every one has the same schema {id,title,severity,where,evidence,impact,suggested_fix,verifier}, so Python over all files gives 62+49+41+44+43+73+45+30. Issue ids exist in three unlinked layers. adopter-clarity's findings.json uses slugs ('prime-documents-removed-verdict-record'). Its report table re-ids them as M1..m30, and report.md:109 lists the source slugs of one M row. Issues then carry the M/m ids only inside the title, as '(M1-M5, M10, M12, m1-m11)' or '(m3-m8, m22, m24, m26)'. Report-local ids collide: F1 exists in both docs-consistency and release-readiness. Because `new` cannot write a body, the finding went into Evidence as prose ('FINDING (high, Horde, fix-incomplete…) Where: … Proof: … Sceptic's check: …', translated from Polish, issue 129) or as one shared pointer line pasted 13 times ('Source: …/report.md (ids in the title)', translated from Polish). No command can answer 'which of the 437 findings have an issue, and which were deliberately left out'.
proposal: Add `jarl.mjs import <findings.json> [--source <report dir>] [--group-by <field>] [--dry-run]`. It maps each surviving finding to an issue: where→**Where:**, evidence→## What, impact→## Why, suggested_fix→## Acceptance (as a proposal line), severity→prio (blocker/high→1, medium/major→2, low/minor→3). It writes a new header field **Source:** <report-dir>#<finding id>, which is globally stable because the report directory name is dated and unique. Import is idempotent: a finding whose Source already exists is skipped. `--group-by` supports the observed pattern of several findings per issue, with Source as a list. Add `jarl.mjs sources <findings.json>` to print every finding id with its issue number, or 'unfiled'. Filing none is then recorded explicitly with `set <id> dropped` on a stub, or with a `decide` naming the ids. Cost: about 150 lines of zero-dependency Node plus tests, and a one-paragraph schema contract for findings.json in the research workflow (it already matches). Success measure: a re-run of the 6.1.0 import gives 0 issues with an empty What/Where, and `sources` accounts for 437/437 findings. Replaying the 2026-09-23 import on a scratch copy produces the same issue set with no manual title-encoding.

v.reason: The primary item for research→issue linkage (absorbs A3). The evidence is sound: findings.json files share one schema, ids live only in titles, and `new` cannot write a body. Idempotent import keyed by `<report-dir>#<id>` gives a globally stable source. Add A3's `brief` generator and its 203-209 misnumbering incident as the strongest evidence. Watch-out: import must run under the A1 lock, or it reproduces the duplicate-number race at exactly the moment of bulk filing.

title: Issues filed at scale have no body: `new` cannot write What/Why/Acceptance, and Files is optional, so `next` and the reviewer have nothing to hold
where: jarl.mjs:297-316 (cmdNew flags), :411-414 (acceptanceLineCount, no caller), :478-495 (cmdNext); SKILL.md:43-46, :145-147; issues 089-231
evidence: Python over issues/*.md: 143 issues have empty ## What, ## Acceptance and **Where:**, namely every one from 089 to 231. 34 have an empty **Files:**, including 129-149, the workflow audit batch that ran in parallel. `new` accepts only --kind/--prio/--tier/--tags/--files/--repo/--found-by, and SKILL.md:43 says the state moves 'through one tool… never through a hand edit', so bulk filers stopped editing bodies. `acceptanceLineCount` (jarl.mjs:411) has no caller anywhere in skills/, an intended 'one row per acceptance line' check that was never wired up. The reviewer brief (SKILL.md:145-147, :222) asks whether 'the acceptance line is met literally', and on 143 issues there is no line to check. In cmdNext an issue with no Files has no keys, so it never waits and never blocks. `next` today offers 022 as ready although 022's own acceptance forbids starting it.
proposal: (a) Add `--what`, `--why`, `--where`, `--acceptance` (repeatable) and `--body-from <file>` to `new`, plus `body <id> --section <s> "<text>"` for later edits, so the one-tool rule covers bodies too. (b) `set <id> in-progress` refuses an issue with an empty Acceptance and, in a loop with more than one in-progress issue, an empty Files, naming the command that fills it. This uses the same kind of refusal `done` already has for evidence and review (jarl.mjs:341-342). It is a refusal on the loop's own record, not a landing gate on code. (c) Either wire up acceptanceLineCount as a warning in `set done` when there are fewer --ran/--saw rows than acceptance lines, or delete it. Cost: about 60 lines plus tests, and a SKILL.md paragraph. title: Light worker leases: who, where and since when on every in-progress issue, with stale detection but no automatic takeover
where: jarl.mjs cmdSet:335-355 (the 'why' goes only to the log); cmdBranches:713-730; the ruling worktrees-outside-tmp; a working note of 2026-09-21; `jarl.mjs branches` output
evidence: 87 of 220 done issues never passed through in-progress (Python over '→ in-progress'/'→ done' log lines), so `next` never saw them in flight. Examples are 006-009, 014-020 and 028-040. When one is set, the owner and worktree live only in the log's free-text reason. On 2026-09-21 the OS wiped the system temporary directory, and six workers' worktrees and uncommitted work went with them (a working note of 2026-09-21, ruling worktrees-outside-tmp). Nothing in the loop knew which issues had lost their worker. Today `branches` lists 30+ jarl/* branches at '+0' belonging to done issues (Grain jarl/079…135 with no worktree; ~/.jarl-wt/Grain-223/229/230 and Horde-190/212/221/224 still checked out), and it does not say 'issue done, safe to delete'. proposal: `set <id> in-progress --by <agent> --worktree <path> [--branch <b>]` writes **Worker:**, **Worktree:** and **Since:** into the header, and `set done|dropped|deferred|open` clears them. `status` and `branches` mark an in-progress issue as 'stale' when its worktree path is missing, or when its branch has no commit newer than N hours (default 6, from goal.md). They mark a branch 'done → delete' when its issue is done and the branch is merged. `next` refuses nothing new. A stale lease is shown for the jarl to act on, with no expiry and no automatic takeover (that is Horde's territory lease, see B11). Cost: about 90 lines plus tests.
